items.title: Phil Schaap interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 9, 2003
items.q: And of course Alexander Hamilton went to Columbia you know.

ctx.x: Oh well yeah, this is my connection to Hamilton. When I was — first launched the Countsmen, the Basie alumni band, I briefly — we had a good first year. If I thought that that was going to be the best year, this interview would never have happened. And one of the things is I created a college circuit for us so we would go to these college — right around the time the concept of the college circuit, which it fortified, among other things, Louis Armstrong and the All-Stars and Dave Brubeck and blah-blah-blah was…

Kennedy loved it. Of course why wouldn’t he, but I mean it wasn’t the playing or the song but the whole riff. And so that’s the band. And we, Columbia University Marching band is known for launching what is now a little bit more known which are these novelty orchestras that get pretty wild and non-musical, that the intellectual colleges do for their halftime shows. And when I got to Hamilton I discovered that they had one too. And it was even a little bit more skiffle than ours. It was the Aaron Burr Lucky Shot…
I see. And what year was this again?
